sections.title: class Person, class Product
sections.body:
```python
@dataclass
class Person:
    name: str
    age: int
    email: str

person1 = Person("Alice", 30, "alice@example.com")
person2 = Person("Bob", 25, "bob@example.com")

print(f"Person 1: {person1}")
print(f"Person 2: {person2}")
print(f"Equal: {person1 == person2}")
print(f"As dict: {asdict(person1)}")
print(f"As tuple: {astuple(person1)}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 2: Dataclass with Default Values
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 2: Dataclass with Default Values")
print("=" * 70)

@dataclass
class Product:
    name: str
    price: float
    quantity: int = 0
    in_stock: bool = True
    tags: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

product1 = Product("Laptop", 999.99)
product2 = Product("Mouse", 29.99, 50, True, ["electronics", "accessories"])

print(f"Product 1: {product1}")
print(f"Product 2: {product2}")

# Modify tags safely
product1.tags.append("computers")
product2.tags.append("peripherals")
print(f"Product 1 tags: {product1.tags}")
print(f"Product 2 tags: {product2.tags}")
```

sections.title: class Point, class Rectangle, class Employee
sections.body:
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Point:
    x: float
    y: float

    def distance_from_origin(self) -> float:
        return (self.x**2 + self.y**2) ** 0.5

point = Point(3.0, 4.0)
print(f"Point: {point}")
print(f"Distance from origin: {point.distance_from_origin()}")

try:
    point.x = 5.0
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Cannot modify frozen dataclass: {type(e).__name__}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 4: Post-Init Processing
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 4: Post-Init Processing")
print("=" * 70)

@dataclass
class Rectangle:
    width: float
    height: float
    area: float = field(init=False)
    perimeter: float = field(init=False)

    def __post_init__(self):
        self.area = self.width * self.height
        self.perimeter = 2 * (self.width + self.height)

rect = Rectangle(5.0, 10.0)
print(f"Rectangle: {rect}")
print(f"Area: {rect.area}")
print(f"Perimeter: {rect.perimeter}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 5: Dataclass Inheritance
# ============================================================================
```

sections.title: class Student
sections.body:
```python
@dataclass(order=True)
class Student:
    sort_index: float = field(init=False, repr=False)
    name: str
    grade: float
    age: int = field(compare=False)

    def __post_init__(self):
        self.sort_index = self.grade

students = [
    Student("Alice", 85.5, 20),
    Student("Bob", 92.0, 21),
    Student("Charlie", 78.0, 19),
    Student("Diana", 95.0, 20),
]

print("Original order:")
for s in students:
    print(f"  {s}")

print("\nSorted by grade:")
for s in sorted(students):
    print(f"  {s}")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 7: Pydantic Basic Usage
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 7: Pydantic Basic Usage")
print("=" * 70)

try:
    from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

    class User(BaseModel):
        name: str
        age: int
        email: str
        is_active: bool = True

    # Valid user
    user1 = User(name="Alice", age=30, email="alice@example.com")
    print(f"User 1: {user1}")
    print(f"As dict: {user1.model_dump()}")
    print(f"As JSON: {user1.model_dump_json()}")

    # Type coercion
    user2 = User(name="Bob", age="25", email="bob@example.com")
    print(f"User 2 (age coerced): {user2}")
    print(f"Age type: {type(user2.age)}")

    # Validation error
    try:
        user3 = User(name="Charlie", age="invalid", email="charlie@example.com")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Validation error: {e}")

except ImportError:
    print("Pydantic not installed. Run: pip install pydantic")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 8: Pydantic with Validators
# ============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 8: Pydantic with Validators")
print("=" * 70)

try:
    from pydantic import BaseModel, validator, Field

    class User(BaseModel):
        username: str = Field(..., min_length=3, max_length=20)
        email: str
        age: int = Field(..., ge=18, le=150)
        password: str

        @validator("email")
        def validate_email(cls, v):
            if "@" not in v or "." not in v:
                raise ValueError("Invalid email format")
            return v.lower()

        @validator("password")
        def validate_password(cls, v):
            if len(v) < 8:
                raise ValueError("Password must be at least 8 characters")
            return v

    # Valid user
    user = User(
        username="alice123", email="Alice@Example.com", age=25, password="SecurePass123"
    )
    print(f"Valid user: {user}")
    print(f"Email normalized: {user.email}")

    # Invalid email
    try:
        user2 = User(username="bob", email="invalid", age=25, password="password123")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Invalid email error: {e}")

except ImportError:
    print("Pydantic not installed.")

# ============================================================================
# EXAMPLE 9: Nested Models

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("EXAMPLE 9: Nested Models")
```

sections.title: class Order
sections.body:
```python
@dataclass
class Order:
    order_id: str
    customer_name: str
    items: List[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    total: float = 0.0
    status: str = "pending"
    created_at: datetime = field(default_factory=datetime.now)

    def add_item(self, item_name: str, price: float, quantity: int):
        item = {
            "name": item_name,
            "price": price,
            "quantity": quantity,
            "subtotal": price * quantity,
        }
        self.items.append(item)
        self.calculate_total()

    def calculate_total(self):
        self.total = sum(item["subtotal"] for item in self.items)

    def mark_completed(self):
        self.status = "completed"

order = Order("ORD-001", "Alice")
order.add_item("Laptop", 999.99, 1)
order.add_item("Mouse", 29.99, 2)
order.add_item("Keyboard", 79.99, 1)

print(f"Order ID: {order.order_id}")
print(f"Customer: {order.customer_name}")
print(f"Items: {len(order.items)}")
for item in order.items:
    print(f"  - {item['name']}: ${item['subtotal']:.2f}")
print(f"Total: ${order.total:.2f}")
print(f"Status: {order.status}")
print(f"Created: {order.created_at}")

# ============================================================================
```

sections.title: class Config
sections.body:
```python
@dataclass
class Config:
    name: str
    debug: bool = False
    max_connections: int = field(default=100, metadata={"unit": "connections"})
    timeout: float = field(default=30.0, metadata={"unit": "seconds"})
    _internal: str = field(default="internal", repr=False)

config = Config("MyApp", debug=True)
print(f"Config: {config}")
print(f"Internal field exists but hidden: {config._internal}")

# Access field metadata
from dataclasses import fields

for f in fields(Config):
    if f.metadata:
        print(f"Field {f.name}: {f.metadata}")
```

sections.title: class DataclassUser
sections.body:
```python
@dataclass
class DataclassUser:
    name: str
    age: int
    email: str

# Create many instances
n = 10000

# Dataclass performance
start = time.time()
for i in range(n):
    user = DataclassUser(f"User{i}", i % 100, f"user{i}@example.com")
dataclass_time = time.time() - start

print(f"Dataclass creation time ({n} instances): {dataclass_time:.4f}s")

try:
    from pydantic import BaseModel

    class PydanticUser(BaseModel):
        name: str
        age: int
        email: str

    # Pydantic performance
    start = time.time()
    for i in range(n):
        user = PydanticUser(name=f"User{i}", age=i % 100, email=f"user{i}@example.com")
    pydantic_time = time.time() - start

    print(f"Pydantic creation time ({n} instances): {pydantic_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"Dataclass is {pydantic_time/dataclass_time:.2f}x faster")
    print("(But Pydantic provides validation!)")

except ImportError:
    print("Pydantic not installed for comparison")

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
print("All examples completed!")
print("=" * 70)
```
